name: tc.cave_stalactite r2 A1
label: dungeon/tc.cave_stalactite.r2.A1
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

refSet.reason: 칩셋 dungeon 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: stalactite cluster hanging from the ceiling edge (rock mass tapering to points)

answer.evidence: The object is a wall-mounted cave stalactite cluster seen face-on. The silhouette is widest at the top (rows 0-4, width 48 down to 28) and tapers to a point at row 14. No ellipse, edge line or eave shadow marks a horizontal surface. Rows 0-1 are a flat band at the ceiling attachment, and it is the hanging rock's own face with no front-edge line. The tapering spikes and dark crevice lines are vertical face detail. Because the object is wall-mounted and flat, it reads as a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small row of grey-brown stalactites with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. Each spike reads as about 3 tones (light face, mid, dark edge), so shading is shallow next to the 5-6 steps in the hedge, well and stall. The measured facts are mostly uninformative: tones per tile are 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, and flat coverage is 0%. The 51% neutral share of dark edge pixels means the outline is mixed and partly greyish, with little material tint. By eye the spikes are thin and sparse, with no per-rock facets, grain, speckle or highlight clusters. They look flatter and more sticker-like than the well's stonework or the hedge's leaf clumps. A careful artist would not accept them next to the references because they look thinner and less textured.

surfaces.part: cave ceiling rock band with stalactites hanging from it

answer.evidence: The object is a wall-mounted cluster of stalactites. A wide rock band spans the top rows 0-1 at width 48, then tapers to a point by row 14. The silhouette narrows steadily from 48 to 1 with no widening and narrowing, so there is no ellipse. No row ends in a front-edge line with an eave shadow, and no contents or roof plane are visible. The shaded vertical streaks (dark at x=12 rows 2-8) read as hanging spikes seen face-on. It is a flat front-facing drawing, which suits a wall-mounted kind, and it shows no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of small stalactites with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. Each spike shows about 3 tones: a light top band, a mid body and a darker tip. The references (hedge, well, stall) show 5-6 steps per material with per-element highlights and grain. The stalactites look thin and sticker-like beside them, with little per-spike shading or rock texture such as chips, cracks or speckle. The dark edge pixels are about 51% neutral, which is mixed and gives no clear material-tone outline. The piece is sparse, so the per-tile facts are 0 and cannot be used against it. Judged by eye it is still visibly shallower and flatter than the same-kind references, so it fails.

surfaces.part: stalactite cluster body (hanging cones with dark shadow streaks)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is widest at rows 2-4 (width 28-31) and tapers steadily to a point at row 14. Rows 0-1 are a flat attachment strip, 48 wide, with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The cones are drawn face-on with vertical dark streaks, and no ellipse or horizontal surface appears anywhere. It reads as a flat hanging elevation mounted on the ceiling or wall, with no visible top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of small stalactites with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. It shows about 3 lightness steps (a light highlight, a mid tone and a dark edge) where the Beodeul props use 5-6. The stalactites are thin and sparse, so the per-tile measures are 0 and do not count against it. By eye, though, each spike is a narrow tapered wedge with little grain, no per-form speckle and no stone-by-stone shading. The references (well, stall, hedge) have clustered texture dots and several tones per material. About half of the dark edge pixels are neutral (51%), so the outline is partly tinted and partly grey-black, which I read as mixed. Next to the references it looks thinner, flatter and more sticker-like, and the shading and texture fall short of the Beodeul standard.

surfaces.part: ceiling attachment band at top of stalactite cluster

answer.evidence: The silhouette is 48 px wide at rows 0-1 and tapers to a point at row 14, so it is a row of hanging cones. Column scans show only vertical shading, with dark crack lines at x=12 and light and dark stripes at x=35. No front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse, roof plane or visible contents appear anywhere. The object is a flat front view mounted on the wall or ceiling. Nothing in it calls for a horizontal top surface, so it reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of small stalactites drawn with only 6 distinct colours in total, against 11-40 for the references. That gives roughly 3 lightness steps on the rock, where Beodeul uses about 5-6 per material. The forms read as thin tan or grey spikes with little per-spike modelling, no clustered grain, no speckle and no stone-by-stone shading. The sheet is too small to fill a 16x16 tile, so the tile-density fact is 0 and I judged by eye. Next to the well, stall and hedge it looks thinner, flatter and more sticker-like. The edge pixels are about half neutral, so the outline is mixed, with no clear dark tint of the rock tone. Near-flat coverage is 0%, but only because the spikes are so small. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references.
